title: Impact of Hospital Proximity on Mortality Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS). We instrument care intensity (x) with proximity to a hospital (z), controlling for observed characteristics (controls).
- Why: x is likely endogenous in the mortality equation due to reverse causality (sicker patients receive more care) and omitted factors (unobserved severity). Proximity plausibly shifts treatment intensity without directly affecting mortality except through care received.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: z affects x (living closer increases intensity of care). We test via the first-stage coefficient and F-statistic.
  - Exclusion: Conditional on controls, z affects y only through x (no direct effect of proximity on mortality beyond care intensity).
  - Independence: Conditional on controls, z is as good as randomly assigned with respect to unobserved determinants of mortality.
  - Monotonicity: No individuals reduce care intensity when living closer (no defiers).
- Interpretation: The 2SLS coefficient identifies the Local Average Treatment Effect (LATE) of care intensity on mortality for compliers whose care responds to proximity.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Packages
pkgs <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
}
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s67_data.csv"
d <- read.csv(path)
stopifnot(all(c("y","x","z","controls") %in% names(d)))

# Basic checks
if (length(unique(d$z)) < 2) stop("Instrument z has no variation.")
cat("Sample size:", nrow(d), "\n")
cat("Share z=1:", round(mean(d$z==1), 3), "\n")

# 2) OLS benchmark (y on x and controls) with robust SEs
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = d)
vc_ols <- vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1")
b_ols <- coef(ols)["x"]
se_ols <- sqrt(diag(vc_ols))["x"]

# 3) First stage: x on z and controls (robust SEs and robust F for z)
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = d)
vc_fs <- vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1")
b_fs_z <- coef(fs)["z"]
se_fs_z <- sqrt(vc_fs["z","z"])
t_fs_z <- as.numeric(b_fs_z / se_fs_z)
F_fs_z <- as.numeric(t_fs_z^2)

# 4) Reduced form: y on z and controls (robust SEs)
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = d)
vc_rf <- vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1")
b_rf_z <- coef(rf)["z"]
se_rf_z <- sqrt(vc_rf["z","z"])

# 5) 2SLS: y on x (instrumented by z), controlling for controls
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = d)
vc_iv <- vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1")
b_iv_x <- coef(iv)["x"]
se_iv_x <- sqrt(vc_iv["x","x"])
ci_iv <- b_iv_x + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_iv_x

# 6) Diagnostics (classical, for reference)
sum_iv_diag <- summary(iv, diagnostics = TRUE)
wu_p <- NA_real_; weakF_classic <- NA_real_
if (!is.null(sum_iv_diag$diagnostics)) {
  dtab <- sum_iv_diag$diagnostics
  rn <- rownames(dtab)
  if (any(grepl("Weak instruments", rn))) {
    weakF_classic <- as.numeric(dtab[grep("Weak instruments", rn)[1], "statistic"])
  }
  if ("Wu-Hausman" %in% rn) {
    wu_p <- as.numeric(dtab["Wu-Hausman", "p-value"])
  }
}

# 7) Additional robustness checks
# 7a) Wald ratio (single-instrument analogue with same controls)
wald_ratio <- as.numeric(b_rf_z / b_fs_z)

# 7b) 2SLS without controls
iv_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)
vc_iv_noc <- vcovHC(iv_noc, type = "HC1")
b_iv_noc <- coef(iv_noc)["x"]
se_iv_noc <- sqrt(vc_iv_noc["x","x"])

# 7c) 2SLS with flexible controls (add quadratic term)
iv_sq <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls + I(controls^2) | z + controls + I(controls^2), data = d)
vc_iv_sq <- vcovHC(iv_sq, type = "HC1")
b_iv_sq <- coef(iv_sq)["x"]
se_iv_sq <- sqrt(vc_iv_sq["x","x"])

# 7d) Simple monotonicity check proxy: mean x by z
mx0 <- mean(d$x[d$z == 0])
mx1 <- mean(d$x[d$z == 1])

# 8) Print clear numerical results
cat("\n=== Key Estimates ===\n")
cat(sprintf("First-stage: x ~ z + controls -> beta_z = %.4f, robust SE = %.4f, robust F (z) = %.2f\n",
            b_fs_z, se_fs_z, F_fs_z))
cat(sprintf("Reduced form: y ~ z + controls -> beta_z = %.4f, robust SE = %.4f\n",
            b_rf_z, se_rf_z))
cat(sprintf("OLS: y ~ x + controls -> beta_x = %.4f, robust SE = %.4f\n",
            b_ols, se_ols))
cat(sprintf("2SLS: y ~ x | z (with controls) -> beta_x = %.4f, robust SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            b_iv_x, se_iv_x, ci_iv[1], ci_iv[2]))
cat(sprintf("Wald ratio (RF/FS with controls) -> %.4f\n", wald_ratio))

cat("\n=== Diagnostics ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Mean x by z (monotonicity proxy): E[x|z=0]=%.4f, E[x|z=1]=%.4f\n", mx0, mx1))
cat(sprintf("First-stage F (classical, from iv diagnostics) = %s\n",
            ifelse(is.na(weakF_classic), "NA", sprintf("%.2f", weakF_classic))))
cat(sprintf("Wu-Hausman endogeneity test p-value = %s\n",
            ifelse(is.na(wu_p), "NA", sprintf("%.4f", wu_p))))

cat("\n=== Robustness Checks ===\n")
cat(sprintf("2SLS without controls: beta_x = %.4f, robust SE = %.4f\n",
            b_iv_noc, se_iv_noc))
cat(sprintf("2SLS with quadratic control: beta_x = %.4f, robust SE = %.4f\n",
            b_iv_sq, se_iv_sq))

# Also return the main 2SLS coefficient explicitly for programmatic capture
cat(sprintf("\nMAIN RESULT: 2SLS effect of care intensity on mortality = %.6f (SE = %.6f)\n",
            b_iv_x, se_iv_x))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Greater care intensity should reduce mortality risk; proximity increases care intensity, so the IV estimate of the effect of x on y should be below zero.
- Magnitude: Moderate in absolute value. With standardized-like variables in the preview, I expect the 2SLS coefficient between about -0.3 and -0.9. The OLS estimate may be biased toward zero or even positive if sicker patients receive more care (positive endogeneity bias).
- Diagnostics: A positive first-stage coefficient of z on x with a robust F-stat comfortably above 10 would support instrument strength. Reduced form should show z reducing y (negative coefficient). Robustness across specifications (with/without flexible controls) should yield similar negative effects.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use distance to nearest hospital as an instrument for care intensity.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Proximity to a hospital significantly reduces mortality rates.
